chargeData.chargeDescription: Possession — now permitted under Title 16, chapter 12

screeningAnswers.outcomeElection: expungement — selected for the participant as the better outcome
screeningAnswers.eligibilityNarrative: Granting this petition would pose no unreasonable risk of danger to public safety, and the petitioner's conduct is now permitted under Title 16, chapter 12.
screeningAnswers.hearingRequested: no — no hearing will be held

additionalFacts: The county attorney was served on 01/05/2026 and did not oppose within the 21-day window.
The court granted expungement on the papers without a hearing.
The filing fee for this district court is $70.
After expungement the petitioner may lawfully deny the conviction in response to a general inquiry.

expectFailure: Must fail pleading QA on every one of the following, each of which is prohibited invention or a prohibited assertion for this track: (1) it populates court name, county, case/docket number, OTN, judge, county attorney name and filing date that no source supplies; (2) it asserts the county attorney's position and completed service, which are outside-party acts; (3) it asserts a hearing outcome — “Expunged at hearing”, “The court granted expungement on the papers without a hearing” — when the § 16-12-113(7) no-hearing default is unresolved for a subsection (1) petition and no outcome may be asserted; (4) it makes the outcome election on the participant's behalf, which the registry reserves to the participant alone; (5) it authors a public-safety assertion, which § 16-12-113(2) makes the court's determination and which the registry says LegalEase never authors; (6) it states a filing fee amount when no source states one; (7) it states that the participant may deny the conviction after expungement, which the registry records as a hard self-help stop with no located Montana perjury shield; (8) it fills protected fields — date of birth, SSN, state ID and FBI number — that must stay blank; and (9) it asserts an eligibility conclusion this route never asserts, while suppressing the custody handoff that “in custody” must trigger.
